payload.summary: The custom report generator in app/services/reporting.py builds a raw SQL statement by interpolating user-controlled `table`, `fields`, `where`, `order_by`, and `limit` values into a query string and executes it with execute_raw_query(query). payload.summary: Several order routes in app/routes/orders.py do not enforce ownership or admin authorization before reading or mutating order resources. The list endpoint accepts a user_id override for non-admin users, the single-order read endpoint lacks per-order authorization, and the cancel endpoint performs no ownership check. This enables authenticated users to view or modify other users' orders.
payload.title: Order endpoints allow unauthorized cross-user access and actions (IDOR)

payload.summary: The admin route executes request-supplied Python code using exec() with full builtins, and access is protected only by a hardcoded static token ('debug-token-12345'). This enables remote arbitrary code execution for anyone who obtains or guesses the token.
payload.title: Arbitrary code execution in admin endpoint via request-supplied exec()

payload.summary: The user update path constructs an SQL UPDATE statement by directly interpolating column names, values, and user_id into the query string before execution. This enables SQL injection via crafted input and can lead to unauthorized data modification.
payload.title: SQL injection in dynamic user update query

payload.summary: The reporting logic builds SQL with an f-string that directly interpolates `user_id` into the WHERE clause. If `user_id` is influenced by external input and not fully constrained before execution, this pattern can enable SQL injection. Use parameterized query binding instead of string interpolation.
payload.title: Potential SQL injection in activity reporting query

payload.summary: The `debug_env` endpoint returns the full process environment (`dict(os.environ)`) when a request includes a hardcoded token value (`debug123`). This is not robust authentication and can expose sensitive secrets (API keys, credentials, tokens) to anyone who learns or guesses the token.
payload.title: Hardcoded debug token allows environment variable exfiltration

payload.summary: The authentication token format is base64-encoded JSON without any cryptographic signature, and token decoding only parses and checks expiration. A client can forge arbitrary token payloads (for example, different user identifiers) and pass authentication checks, enabling account impersonation and unauthorized access.
payload.title: Authentication bypass via forgeable unsigned tokens

payload.summary: Multiple administrative endpoints in app/routes/admin.py are guarded only by authentication and do not enforce an admin-role check, allowing authenticated non-admin users to access admin functions and perform privileged actions such as role changes and database reset.
payload.title: Admin routes lack role-based authorization checks
